# ADR-0010: A paper that carries names is committed unchanged under an approved exception

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | accepted |
| **Date** | 2026-10-19 |
| **Deciders** | the Operator; proposed by the inter |

## Context

The iteration package (ADR-0008) keeps every earlier white paper unchanged. The first paper,
"From Seed to Tree", reached this repository as an HTML file generated by the office iteration
(`docs/iterations/papers/01-from-seed-to-tree.html`). It names the Operator and their job title,
names a client, and describes client work. This repository is public, and its rule is that
nothing committed names a person or holds content from a client; the commit-time forbidden-words
guard (`devhost-verify`) enforces it against the ignored `.devhost/redact-names.txt`.

A byte-for-byte copy and the repository's no-names rule cannot both hold without a way for the
Operator to approve a named exception. The paper itself argues that every guardrail needs an
exception path whose owner signs off.

## Decision

The original paper is committed byte for byte, with its sha256 recorded in the papers folder's
README. Next to it sits a Markdown copy marked "derived" for agents, in which the diagrams keep
only their captions.

The forbidden-words guard skips the files listed in `.devhost/name-exceptions.txt`, a list the
Operator approves. Every other file is still checked. The exception is by file, never by word,
and a new entry is the Operator's decision. A test shows the guard still refuses a listed word
in an unlisted file, and fails against the guard without the exception code.

## Options considered

### Option 1: the original stays out of git, a cleaned copy is committed

The original would sit in the package folder, ignored by git, with its hash recorded; the
committed copy would say "the Operator". It lost because the package would then be complete only
on one machine, and the paper would no longer be kept as DSNP received it.

### Option 2: commit it unchanged, as an exception the Operator approves (chosen)

It keeps the paper unchanged and the package complete in the repository, and it makes the
exception explicit, narrow and reviewable instead of weakening the guard.

### Option 3: the package lives outside this repository

It would go to a private place, with this repository recording only that it exists. It lost
because the package is meant to be the seed the next project starts from, and a seed kept
outside the repository breaks the "everything the way of working needs is in the checkout" rule.

## Consequences

- The paper's names are public once the paper's pull request merges; the Operator accepts that.
- The guard change must merge before the paper, or the guard refuses the paper's files.
- A future paper that names people needs the same approved entry; the list is the audit trail.
- The exception list is a place to look when a name turns up in a public file.
- The guard documentation in the devhost NOTES describes the exception list.
